title: engine check tests the requested engine, not the settings engine
description: Engine Check → CPU crashes the app when the user's selected engine in Settings is still NPU (the default). Root cause: `EngineCheckRunner.run(engine)` ignores the `engine` parameter and calls `TranscriberFactory.create("en")`, and `SherpaTranscriberFactory.create` always reads the engine from settings. So tapping "Check CPU" while settings.asrEngine == "npu" instantiates the NPU recognizer from the CPU bundle's paths and the static init / native ctor can crash. Fix: make the factory accept an explicit engine and have the engine-check path pass it through.
steps: Edit `app/src/main/java/com/convoscribe/asr/TranscriberFactory.kt`: change the `fun interface TranscriberFactory` into a regular interface (keep the name) with `fun create(language: String): StreamingTranscriber = create(language, null)` (default delegates to the engine-aware overload) and `fun create(language: String, engine: String?): StreamingTranscriber`. The default impl of the new overload must throw `UnsupportedOperationException("engine-aware create not implemented")` so it is impossible to forget to override — only `SherpaTranscriberFactory` overrides it. `needsPreparation(language)` keeps its current signature, but the recording controller already reads `factory.needsPreparation(lang)` before calling the old single-arg overload so no other call sites change.

Edit `app/src/main/java/com/convoscribe/engine/sherpa/SherpaTranscriberFactory.kt`: override the new `create(language, engine)`. Logic: let `engine = engine ?: settings.settings.value.asrEngine`; continue with the existing bundle selection, model dir resolution, NPU preparation and backend construction. When `engine` is explicitly `null` keep the current behaviour; when it is `"npu"` or `"cpu"` honour it (so the engine check can override the settings). Update the kdoc.

Edit `app/src/main/java/com/convoscribe/enginecheck/EngineCheckRunner.kt`: change `run(engine)` to call `factory.create("en", engine)` (the two-arg overload). Update the kdoc to say the factory is given the requested engine so the result reflects the engine that was tested.

Edit `app/src/main/java/com/convoscribe/ui/enginecheck/EngineCheckViewModel.kt`: the `EngineCheckRunnerFactory` `create(sampleFile, clock)` lambda currently captures `container.transcriberFactory`. Add a second overload `create(sampleFile, clock, engine)` that captures an engine-pinned factory. In `runCheck(engine)`, build the runner through the new overload. Easiest path: pass `engine` through to `runnerFactory.create(sampleFile, clock, engine)` and have the lambda construct an inline `TranscriberFactory` wrapper that forwards `create(lang, requestedEngine)` to `container.transcriberFactory.create(lang, requestedEngine)`. No production read of `settings.asrEngine` inside the engine-check code path remains.

* `app/src/test/java/com/convoscribe/enginecheck/EngineCheckRunnerTest.kt`: add `run_forwardsRequestedEngineToFactory` — a `RecordingFactory` records the `engine` parameter passed to `create("en", engine)` and asserts it equals `"cpu"` (and a second test with `"npu"`).

* `app/src/test/java/com/convoscribe/enginecheck/EngineCheckRunnerTest.kt`: add `run_factoryIgnoresSettingsEngine_succeedsForBothEngines` — two scenarios in one test method (parameterised via a tiny loop): the runner is given a factory whose `create(lang, engine)` returns a different fake transcriber for each engine; the runner records which one it received; assert the recorder shows the requested engine, not a settings read.

* `app/src/test/java/com/convoscribe/engine/sherpa/SherpaTranscriberFactoryTest.kt` (new file, Robolectric so the `SettingsRepository` SharedPreferences can be wired): pin the new behaviour. Three cases: (a) `create("en", null)` reads from settings (current behaviour preserved); (b) `create("en", "cpu")` with settings.asrEngine == "npu" produces a CPU backend (assert by inspecting the recognizer config's `provider` — `"cpu"` vs `"qnn"`); (c) `create("en", "npu")` with settings.asrEngine == "cpu" produces an NPU backend. Use Robolectric's `RuntimeEnvironment` for the `Context`, set the language + engine through `SettingsRepository`. The `OnlineRecognizer` ctor hits the native library, so build a fake `RecognizerBackendFactory` interface in front of `SherpaRecognizerBackend` (extract the backend-construction step into a tiny package-internal function `fun buildBackend(engine: String, ...): RecognizerBackend` and let the test replace it via a `@VisibleForTesting` factory seam if needed) — make sure the test does not load `libsherpa-onnx-jni.so`. If a clean extraction is too invasive, fall back to asserting that `SherpaAsrConfigs.cpu(...)` vs `npu(...)` was called: keep a `var lastProvider: String? = null` in a tiny `object ProviderProbe` set inside the factory and read it from the test.
acceptanceCriteria: Running the engine check with the user's settings.asrEngine == "npu" and the CPU bundle installed, then tapping "Check CPU", builds a CPU recognizer (verified by `SherpaAsrConfigs.lastProvider == "cpu"` in the test) and the runner's recorded `create` arg equals `"cpu"`
Symmetric case: settings.asrEngine == "cpu", bundle NPU installed, tapping "Check NPU" builds an NPU recognizer (provider `"qnn"`) and the recorded arg equals `"npu"`
Existing `runCheck("cpu")` behaviour with settings.asrEngine == "cpu" still works (no regression in the regression test in `EngineCheckRunnerTest`)
All existing tests in `EngineCheckRunnerTest` still pass unchanged
`source scripts/env.sh && ./gradlew ktlintCheck testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug` exits 0
notes: Files to read first: `asr/TranscriberFactory.kt`, `engine/sherpa/SherpaTranscriberFactory.kt`, `enginecheck/EngineCheckRunner.kt`, `ui/enginecheck/EngineCheckViewModel.kt`. The recording controller does not need to change — its single-argument call still resolves to the engine-aware default. Do not change `SherpaRecognizerBackend` itself, only the factory that builds it. The kdoc on `TranscriberFactory.create(language, engine)` must say that `null` means "use the settings engine" (preserves backwards compatibility for the recording path) and a non-null value forces the engine regardless of settings. Never instantiate `com.k2fsa.sherpa.onnx` engine classes in tests; the only sherpa class touchable from the JVM is `*Config` data classes. Always: run `source scripts/env.sh` before Gradle; the verify command is `source scripts/env.sh && ./gradlew ktlintCheck testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug`; run `./gradlew --stop` before ending.
